messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

**Draft — 2026 in review** (swap the placeholder numbers and names for your real ones)

---

### How the year went

In January a deploy took 41 minutes. Today it takes six. I lead with that because everything else on this list got cheaper once we stopped standing around waiting on it.

Breaking up the monolith took three quarters, not two. That's not on anyone. The billing tables were knottier than the design doc let on, and most of Q2 went to unpicking them before a single service moved. Still the right call: checkout p95 dropped from 900ms to 310ms.

The tally: 1,247 PRs merged. Four incidents at Sev-2 or worse, against eleven last year. On-call grew from six people to nine, which is the unglamorous reason that second number fell.

What we didn't do: clean up feature flags. There are 340 dead ones in the tree, and I have personally bumped that ticket four times. The docs rewrite died in March. If you were waiting on either, that's on me. Both sit on the Q1 list now, and this time each has a name attached.

Two people joined. Welcome, Priya and Sam. One left: Marcus, thank you for the seven years.

My ask for next year is unexciting. Fewer things open at once. We ran five initiatives in parallel and finished three. Three, finished, would have felt better and cost less.

See you Monday.

---
